title: Cross-lane affinity mapper and fused dequant prefetcher for mixed-precision kernels
author: Maya Thompson
description:
Motivation: Quantized inference (INT8/FP8) at production scale is dominated by two things: kernel micro-inefficiencies when lanes compete for the dequant path, and wasted cycles waiting on KV cache tile loads that are not locality-aware. This PR introduces two cooperating runtime optimizations to address those hotspots: a cross-lane affinity mapper that pins logical KV ranges and compute lanes to consistent worker contexts, and a fused dequant prefetcher that stages dequantized tiles into a small software-managed staging buffer so kernels see warm data with reduced memory fanout.

High-level changes (single-string): Added an affinity mapping layer to the kernel runtime that emits lightweight hints to the scheduler (runtime/affinity/mapper.{cc,h}) and exposes a non-breaking opt-in flag (--quant-affinity=on). Implemented a fused dequant prefetch path in runtime/kernel/prefetcher_int8.cc that performs on-the-fly dequant + reorder into a contiguous staging slab sized per-GPU SM cluster. Updated the continuous-batching controller (runtime/scheduler/continuous_batching.rs) to honor affinity hints and prefer batching requests with matching KV affinity, reducing cross-warp memory pressure. Microkernel updates include a small API surface (runtime/kernel/tile_view.h) used by the prefetcher and int8 kernels to map staged tiles with zero-copy when supported.

Performance summary: On internal Llama-65B INT8 and FP8 quant profiles with 2k token windows and mixed request sizes, end-to-end P95 latency decreased by 8-12% and aggregate throughput improved by 16-22% on our CI GPU fleet (A100/A30 mixes). For KV-heavy chat workloads (prefix reuse > 75%) we observe up to 28% reduction in memory bandwidth utilization and 10-15% lower token cost due to fewer kernel stalls. Microbenchmarks included 1k/2k/4k token sweeps across batch sizes 1..32.

Compatibility and rollout: The changes are opt-in by default (quant-affinity=off). We ship with a canary rollout plan: enable on Dedicated dev pools for 48h, monitor token-level latency/CPU/GPU metrics and KV cache hit/miss ratios using Redwood Console dashboards, escalate if regression beyond 3% P95 or new OOMs are observed. No public API changes; SDKs unchanged.

Testing: Added unit tests for affinity mapping logic and prefetcher correctness (tests/affinity_mapper_test.cc, tests/prefetcher_int8_test.py). Added an end-to-end quant perf job to the CI benchmark matrix (benchmarks/quant_canary.yml). Ran extended stress on perf-canary cluster for 72h and validated rollback path.

Safety: Prefetcher includes a per-GPU budget and adaptive backoff; it will disable itself on sustained memory pressure or when kv-cache hit-rate drops below configured threshold. Affinity mapping falls back to existing scheduler behavior if hinting is unsupported or if head_branch config is absent.

Related work: This PR complements recent continuous-batching improvements and kv-cache routing changes (see ENG-1887 and PRs referenced in the linked linear items). It intentionally avoids modifying kernel numerical pathways — dequant semantics are unchanged and validated against float baselines. Refer to linked Linear tasks for rollout playbook and dashboards to watch.

review_comments: Lina Gomez: Great direction — can we add a guard that disables affinity when cross-node KV replication is active? (requested change)
Maya Thompson: Added a guard that checks replication_mode; mapper now falls back to default when replication is async. See mapper.cc lines ~120-140.

Arjun Patel: Initial run showed a flaky perf test; looks like the staging slab sizing underestimated worst-case FP8 tile expansion. Suggest doubling max slab size with adaptive shrink. (requested change)
Maya Thompson: Implemented adaptive sizing with a cap controlled by runtime flag --prefetch-slab-max-mb; updated tests to exercise the cap.
Samir Kaur: Code looks safe; nvprof traces show reduced global loads per token. Approving once CI green. (approved)
CI Bot: perf/quant_bench infra failed on first run due to missing CUDA driver on runner; re-run succeeded. (info)
release_notes: Add cross-lane affinity mapper and fused dequant prefetcher to reduce latency and improve throughput for INT8/FP8 quantized workloads. Opt-in via --quant-affinity flag. Can be enabled progressively via canary rollout.
notes_for_oncall: If enabled in production, watch P95 latency, GPU memory pressure, and KV cache miss-rate. Fallback is automatic on OOM or sustained miss-rate regression; operator can toggle --quant-affinity off at runtime or use the rollout controls in Redwood Console.
benchmarks_summary: P95 -8..-12% across A100/A30 fleet; throughput +16..+22% on representative llm-65b quant workloads; up to 28% memory-bandwidth reduction on KV-heavy traces. Test harness: 72h perf-canary sweep with batch sizes 1..32 and token lengths 1k/2k/4k.
